# demoframe: contract for coding agents

demoframe turns a YAML/JSON config into a polished demo GIF/WebP/MP4 by
rendering HTML templates in Chromium. You (the agent) write the config; the
tool owns the pixels. Rendering is deterministic and local; the only network
use is the one-time, checksum-pinned download of Chromium and gifski.

An MCP server is included: `demoframe-mcp` (stdio) exposes get_schema,
validate_config, list_templates, preview_demo, render_demo, get_report. A Claude Code skill ships at
skills/demoframe/SKILL.md in the package.

## Commands

- `demoframe init [dir] [--template <name>] [--category <name>]
  [--frame phone|browser|terminal] [--list] [--no-agent-instructions]`: scaffold demo.yml + assets/ from a gallery template. --list prints
  the gallery (starters plus showcase templates, shipped in the package under
  templates/). --frame is sugar for --template starter-<frame>; the default is
  starter-phone. Each template's meta.yml records the demoframe version it
  targets. --category chooses a category default unless --template is supplied.
  init also writes/refreshes a sentinel-marked demoframe block in the nearest
  git-root AGENTS.md so consuming agents see the interview rule; pass
  --no-agent-instructions to skip that.
- `demoframe install-agent-instructions [dir]`: idempotently write/refresh the
  demoframe block in the nearest git-root AGENTS.md, falling back to dir when no
  repo root is found.
- `demoframe schema`: print the JSON Schema for configs. It is the authoritative
  source of truth for the config shape; read it instead of relying on memorized
  fields.
- `demoframe check <config> [--strict] [--autonomous] [--allow-raw-screenshots]
  [--for github-readme,x-post,linkedin,product-hunt]`: validate without
  rendering. Exit 0 = valid; exit 1 if there are errors. Errors and warnings print
  with stable finding codes in the API and human messages in the CLI. A missing,
  TODO-filled, inferred, or otherwise unconfirmed brief is an error by default.
  Only --autonomous demotes the brief gate to a notice; it does not demote
  missing assets or other non-brief errors. --strict fails on warnings, not
  notices, so check --autonomous --strict can pass the brief gate while still
  failing real warnings. A frameless demo whose every content scene is a raw
  screenshot is a hard error ("screenshots pasted in a frame") that also makes render
  refuse; pass --allow-raw-screenshots to demote it to a warning for an intentional
  raw demo. When brief.intent is abstract, any screenshot scene is an error unless
  brief.screenshotPolicy is raw-intentional, and rendered scenes must include
  visible product payload from brief.product, brief.verbatimCopy, or a metric/callout
  value; theme.logo alone is not enough. --for applies the same destination presets
  as render for validation, so preset-adjusted policy errors (for example transparent
  MP4/WebM) fail before preview/render. Missing referenced assets are hard errors. Warnings cover privacy findings (emails/tokens/URLs
  in copy), README legibility, brief quality mismatches, and screenshots likely to blow the GIF size budget. Fast (<1s without
  screenshot assets); run after every config edit.
- `demoframe render <config> [-o dir] [--keep-frames] [--no-download] [--no-stills]
  [--allow-raw-screenshots] [--strict] [--autonomous] [--assumption text]
  [--asset-out path]
  [--for github-readme,x-post,linkedin,product-hunt]`:
  the full pipeline. Validates, renders frames, encodes every format in
  output.format, writes preview stills to <dir>/preview/, and writes
  report.json. Missing Chromium/gifski are downloaded automatically
  (--no-download fails fast instead). If a GIF/WebP exceeds output.budget it
  retries at 12fps, then 400px, then reports failure with suggestions.
  --for applies a destination preset that overrides output format/width/fps/
  budget/quality in one flag (github-readme: webp 640px 15fps 4MB; x-post:
  mp4 1080px 30fps; linkedin: mp4 1080px 24fps; product-hunt: gif 1200px
  12fps 3MB). --for accepts a comma list and writes suffixed outputs.
  Overrides are printed and preset names land in report.json. Presets never
  change output.motionBlur. render warns when the requested --for targets do
  not overlap brief.placement. --asset-out copies
  the primary rendered asset(s); when it covers the embeddable GIF/WebP, the
  printed README snippet points at the copied destination.
  --autonomous is the only way to render an unconfirmed brief; the report labels
  it mode: inferred, confirmed: false, and records assumptions from repeatable
  --assumption flags (or brief.assumptions when no flags are supplied). Managed
  files in outDir are staged and promoted only after encode, preview, report,
  and strict layout checks pass. A failed render leaves the prior output,
  preview/, report.json, and .frames cache intact; stale outputs from old
  formats can still remain because promotion only overwrites current managed
  filenames. --asset-out is copied after promotion, so a copy failure can leave
  outDir updated.
- `demoframe preview <config> [-o dir] [--autonomous] [--assumption text]
  [--for github-readme,x-post,linkedin,product-hunt]`: stills only, no encode. Writes
  semantic per-scene stills (scene_<i>_<slug>.png), key moments
  (moment_<i>_tap/cta/celebrate.png), final_readme_size.png, and
  final_github_dark/light.png composites. Transparent configs also write
  final_transparent_checkerboard.png. Faster iteration than render. It refuses
  the same unconfirmed brief gate as render unless --autonomous is passed; it
  echoes inferred assumptions but does not persist a report. --for uses the same
  destination preset settings as render; when multiple presets are supplied, preview
  writes stills for the highest-quality preset, matching render's preview target.
- `demoframe doctor`: environment report. `demoframe install-browser`: explicit
  Chromium download (otherwise automatic on first render).
- `demoframe serve <config> [-p port]`: live preview server with a scrubber (for humans).

## Agent workflow

Before writing YAML, do repo reconnaissance:

- Read the closest README, app/package metadata, route names, existing demos,
  and source screenshots to learn the product vocabulary.
- Identify audience, core workflow, primary objects, final success state, exact
  copy to preserve, and private data to replace.
- Choose frame and destination from the story surface, not only screenshot
  dimensions.

Then create a scene mapping before rendering:

```md
source signal -> intent -> scene -> preserve / simplify / remove / copy
mobile ask screenshot -> user request -> typing -> preserve product name / simplify chrome / remove avatars / copy button label
terminal log -> work being done -> terminal-playback -> preserve command + pass line / simplify middle output / remove hostnames / copy "All checks passed"
PR page -> final result -> status-card -> preserve title + checks / simplify files / remove timestamps / copy "Ready for review"
```

Every source signal must either map to a synthetic scene or be explicitly
treated as an intentional raw screenshot with `brief.screenshotPolicy:
raw-intentional`.

## MCP tools

- `get_schema`: return schema/demoframe.schema.json.
- `validate_config`: structured check result; accepts `for`, `strict`,
  `autonomous`, and `allowRawScreenshots`.
- `list_templates`: return bundled gallery templates with categories, frames,
  scenes, and descriptions.
- `preview_demo`: run destination-aware preview still generation; accepts `for`,
  `autonomous`, `assumptions`, and `noDownload`, and returns written still paths.
- `render_demo`: run render with CLI parity for `for`, `strict`,
  `allowRawScreenshots`, `assetOut`, `autonomous`, `assumptions`, and
  `encoderProfile`; returns report.json.
- `get_report`: read a previous report.json.

## report.json shape

{ "title", "config", "presets"?, "budgetBytes",
  "brief": { "present", "mode": "user-confirmed"|"inferred",
    "confirmed": bool, "requiredComplete", "recommendedComplete",
    "missingRequired": [], "missingRecommended": [], "assumptions"? },
  "cinematic"?: { "ambient"?: { "type": "ember", "scope": "timeline" } },
  "motionBlur": { "requested": "off"|"cinematic"|"force",
    "outputs": [{preset?,format,motionBlur,captureMode,
      policy: "off"|"cinematic"|"gif-cinematic-skip"|"force"|"gif-force"}] },
  "attempts": [{preset?,format,fps,width,motionBlur,captureMode,sizeBytes}],
  "errors": [{code,message}], "warnings": [{code,message}],
  "notices": [{code,message}], "layout": [...],
  "previews": ["preview/scene_0_typing.png", ...],
  "outputs": [{ "file", "format": "gif"|"webp"|"mp4"|"webm",
  "transparent", "transparencyMode": "alpha"|"1-bit"|"none", "sizeBytes",
  "width", "height", "durationS", "fps", "frameCount", "loopsForever",
  "hasAudio", "encoder", "captureMode", "motionBlur", "withinBudget" }] }

Verify after render: brief.confirmed true for normal/human-confirmed demos,
brief.requiredComplete true, brief.recommendedComplete true, withinBudget true,
loopsForever true, durationS as designed. Then read
the preview stills to verify layout: text readable at README size, nothing
clipped, final frame tells the story alone.

## Config schema

Full JSON Schema: `demoframe schema` or schema/demoframe.schema.json (npm package root).

Top level: { title?, output?, theme?, frame, brief?, cinematic?, scenes }

output.motionBlur policy:
- off: every format uses directCapture.
- cinematic: blur-capable formats use blurredCapture for eligible choreography
  windows; GIF is skipped/directCapture and check/render record a notice.
- force: eligible choreography windows use blurredCapture even for GIF. GIF
  force emits a warning about palette, dither, and size tradeoffs, so
  --strict fails before rendering. Force does not mean every frame is blurred,
  and text-mutating scenes remain direct inside the blur capture path.
- Destination presets may override only format, width, fps, budget, and
  quality. They must not implicitly turn on motionBlur or alter the requested
  visual behavior.

brief records the interview that produced the demo and now gates execution.
All fields are optional in the parser so partial briefs can be loaded, but
check/preview/render error when the brief is missing, inferred, incomplete, or
not marked user-confirmed. --autonomous is the explicit opt-out for headless
inference; it demotes only brief.unconfirmed/brief.incomplete to notices and
labels reports as inferred.
Confirmed non-raw reconstruction briefs warn when they omit both brief.product
and brief.repo, or when brief.verbatimCopy has no exact UI copy. These warnings
do not block normal check/render unless --strict is enabled; they exist to keep
agent-authored demos from becoming generic.

brief fields:
- mode user-confirmed|inferred: user-confirmed means the user answered the
  interview and confirmed the screen-to-scene mapping. inferred is an honest
  label, not a bypass; it still requires --autonomous to preview/render.
- audience string: required by check.
- source string: required by check; record source material/provenance such as
  screenshots, app screens, or the product flow being reconstructed.
- screenshotPolicy reconstruct|simplify|raw-intentional: required by check.
  reconstruct/simplify warn when screenshot scenes exceed 50% of runtime;
  raw-intentional warns when there are no screenshot scenes. This does not
  authorize raw screenshot output; --allow-raw-screenshots is still required to
  demote the frameless all-screenshot hard error.
- placement github-readme|x-post|linkedin|product-hunt, or a non-empty list of
  those values: required by check. render --for warns when its requested
  destination set is disjoint from placement; --for still drives output presets.
- arc string and climax string: recommended by the schema docs and required for
  confirmed execution because confirmed means required and recommended fields
  are complete.
- brand?: { accent?: hex, frame?: phone|browser|terminal|desktop|none,
  mode?: light|dark, notes?: string }. check compares accent/mode with the
  resolved theme and frame with config.frame.type.
- product?: string, repo?: string, verbatimCopy?: string[].
- assumptions?: string[] (max 10): optional YAML fallback for autonomous
  inferred runs. CLI/MCP supplied assumptions take precedence; empty strings are
  trimmed/dropped.

Public API note: runCheck/runCheckLoaded return `errors`, `warnings`, and
`notices` as structured findings `{ code, message, details? }` plus
`briefGate?`; older callers that expected string arrays must read `.message`.

output (all optional): format gif|webp|mp4|webm or a list like [webp, mp4]
(gif), width 200-1200 (480), fps 5-30 (15), budget e.g. "5MB" (applies to gif
and webp; mp4/webm encode once without the retry ladder), displayWidth
(README <img> width), quality draft|standard|high (standard; high = 4x
supersampling, slower). Prefer webp for READMEs: GIF-like autoplay at a
fraction of the size, full color. webm is VP9: smaller than mp4 for video
destinations that accept it.

theme (all optional):
- preset github-dark|paper|midnight|candy: a curated accent+mode+palette
  bundle. Explicit theme keys silently override the preset.
- accent hex ("#e2603a" when neither accent nor preset set), mode light|dark
  (light when neither mode nor preset set).
- font: inter|system, or { sans?: path, mono?: path } pointing at local
  .woff2/.ttf files (embedded at render; one file per family serves all
  weights). A missing slot falls back to the bundled Inter / JetBrains Mono.
- logo: path, or { src: path, placement: header|corner (header) }. header puts
  a small logo in the frame's title bar; corner overlays a badge bottom-right
  over the scenes. Falls back to corner when there is no header to use (frame
  type none, or phone without a title).
- palette: partial override of the 11 named slots (page, screen, card, text,
  muted, faint, border, success, successBg, info, shadow), values hex or
  rgb()/rgba(). Applied over the mode/preset palette. Unknown keys are errors.
- background hex: shorthand for palette.page; palette.page wins if both set.

frame: { type: phone, title?, subtitle?, statusBarTime? }
     | { type: browser, url?, title? }
     | { type: terminal, title?, prompt? }
     | { type: desktop, title?, subtitle? }  macOS-style app window
     | { type: none }  frameless: scenes fill the canvas edge-to-edge
Every frame also takes width? and height? (320-1920) overriding the default
canvas: phone 480x1040, browser 960x640, terminal 820x520, desktop 1024x640,
none 960x640. output.width still controls the encoded pixel width; frame
width/height set the canvas shape and aspect. Every frame also takes outside?
("page" default, "transparent", or "#hex"), shadow? (true), and margin? (0-256,
transparent-only padding after alpha trim). Phone alone also takes deviceColor?
(hex) for the bezel.

Transparent output is alpha-based, not chroma-keyed. Use WebP for clean 8-bit
alpha. GIF uses 1-bit transparency, warns, and disables the soft shadow; MP4/WebM
with outside: transparent is a policy error. Use outside: "#hex" when a video or
GIF needs an opaque matte fallback. frame.type none + transparent is allowed but
warns because the rectangular content edge becomes the cutout.

Scenes can override frame chrome with scenes[].frame, but only for fields that
belong to the global frame type: phone title/subtitle/statusBarTime, browser
title/url/chrome, terminal title/prompt, desktop title/subtitle. Global-only
controls such as outside, shadow, margin, and deviceColor are rejected in scene
overrides. Example: browser scene 1 can show a VPS work URL/title, then scene 2
can switch to a GitHub PR URL/title for the result while keeping one browser
frame.

scenes: 1-12 entries, each with duration (seconds, <=30, total <=60),
optional transition cut|crossfade|push|dip-to-color (cut default; crossfade,
push, and dip-to-color each cost GIF size like a fade; push slides the incoming
scene in from the right and falls back to crossfade when chrome differs across
the pair; dip-to-color dips through the theme background at the midpoint),
and optional celebrate?: bool (a restrained success burst, a checkmark pop +
ring + accent dots, anchored to the scene's CTA/result; put it on the final
scene or a trailing hold so it lands on the closing frame):

- typing: { text (<=220 chars), placeholder?, send?: bool }
  Phone/browser: chat composer with typing animation. Terminal: prompt line.
- steps: { header?: {title<=40, detail<=100}, items: 1-6 of
  { label<=60, detail?<=120, state: done|active|pending, link?: bool } }
  Rows appear sequentially with staggered timing.
- status-card: { title<=80, subtitle?<=100, branch?: {from<=60, into<=40},
  checks: 0-4 strings<=60, cta?: {label<=40, style: success|primary|neutral},
  caption?<=120 }  PR/deploy-style result screen.
- screenshot: { src: path relative to config, fit: contain|cover,
  pan: none|up|down|left|right|zoom-in|zoom-out, caption?<=120 }
  Fallback only: use when the screenshot itself is the subject (bug report,
  before/after, dashboard layout), not for polished launch assets. Rebuild
  product flows as synthetic scenes; check warns when screenshots dominate a
  framed demo, and errors (render refuses) when a frameless demo is all raw
  screenshots unless --allow-raw-screenshots is passed.
  Prefer clean UI screenshots; photographic images explode GIF size.
- terminal-playback: { command<=150, output?: 0-10 lines (string or
  {text<=100, style: normal|dim|success|error|warn}), spinner?<=40,
  exit?: {status: success|error, label?<=60}, prompt?<=16 }
  Types the command, shows a spinner while "running", streams output lines,
  then the exit status and a fresh prompt. Native in the terminal frame;
  renders as a mini terminal panel inside phone/browser frames.
- code: { lang: text|bash|typescript|javascript|tsx|jsx|json|yaml|python|go|
  rust|html|css|sql|markdown|diff (text), title?<=60, code (<=1500 chars,
  <=24 lines, <=100 chars/line), added?: [1-based line numbers],
  removed?: [...], lineNumbers?: bool, reveal: lines|fade|none (lines) }
  Syntax-highlighted panel (bundled shiki, github-light/dark per theme.mode).
  added/removed mark diff lines with +/- gutters and tinted backgrounds.
- chat: { messages: 1-6 of {role: user|assistant, text<=200},
  typingIndicator?: bool (true), avatars?: {user?, assistant?} each an image
  path or {initials<=3, color?: hex} }  Conversation bubbles; assistant
  replies show a typing indicator first. Avatars sit beside each row; header
  app identity still comes from theme.logo. Pairs best with the phone frame
  (check warns in a terminal frame).
- metric-card: { title?<=80, metrics: 1-4 of {label<=40, value, prefix?<=8,
  suffix?<=12, decimals: 0-2 (0)}, chart?: {kind: bar|line, series: 2-16
  numbers >=0, labels?: same length as series, each<=12, color?: hex},
  caption?<=120 }  Counters tick up, bars/line reveal, labels fade in last.
- screen: { motion?: reveal|focus|scroll (reveal), layout?: stack|hero|split
  (stack), focus?: block name, blocks: 1-8 fixed product UI blocks } Blocks use
  `block` as the discriminator: app-header, stat-strip, chart-card
  (bar|line|area), card-grid, list, progress, heatmap, callout. Blocks are
  asset-free: icons are built-in keys and avatars are initials/color objects.
  `focus` must name a unique block when motion is focus, and is invalid for
  reveal/scroll.
- hold: {} freezes the previous scene's final state (cannot be first).

Authoring source is exclusive: provide `scenes`, `shots`, or
`brief.story.recipe`, never more than one. Direct
`shots` require story v2 and an explicit profile. Each shot has:

- `id`, `beatId`, `duration`, and 1-8 named `objects`;
- objects with `id`, slot `hero|supporting|background|foreground`, optional
  `carry`, and
  enter/exit `none|fade|slide-up|slide-left|scale` plus emphasis
  `none|focus|pulse`;
- `kind: scene` embeds a non-hold legacy scene. Primitive kinds are
  `kinetic-text` (durable headline copy), `logo-lockup` (product, local mark,
  manifest asset ref), `product-surface` (small semantic state/row model),
  `hero-metric`, `chart-path`, and local `image` (fit, mask, tint, restrained
  parallax). SVG images are sanitized on ingest: scripts, event handlers,
  remote references, `foreignObject`, and embedded assets are removed;
- optional camera `{ target, move: none|push|pan, amount }` where target names
  an authored or carried object;
- transition `{ type: cut|shared-element|masked-wipe|directional, duration,
  direction? }` (direction is required only for directional);
- optional independent ambient window `{ type: none|ember, start, end }` using
  relative shot progress.

Use shots only when coordinated objects or a purposeful focus move clarify the
story. Legacy scenes remain on the untouched renderer. `report.json` includes
the resolved graph, authoring source, render path, and deterministic hash.
See `examples/shots-compositor/demo.yml` and `examples/primitives/demo.yml`.
Prefer the smallest object set that makes causality obvious: a product surface
changing state and one proof object is usually stronger than a decorative
collage.

Recipe authoring uses `{ name, recipeVersion: 1, variant }` under
`brief.story.recipe`. Supported names and explicit variants:

- code-to-result: `evidence-split` | `focused-run`
- problem-to-solution: `resolve-lane` | `state-pair`
- workflow-transformation: `progress-rail` | `handoff-focus`
- metric-proof: `proof-first` | `surface-first`
- ui-focus-tour: `guided-panel` | `persistent-shell`
- architecture-flow: `flow-split` | `system-focus`

Recipe mode requires the first proof relationship to include deterministic
`display` copy. The compiler generates the profile-specific beat skeleton and
ordinary compositor shots. `report.json.shotGraph.recipe` records recipe,
version, variant, beat sequence, composition family, motif, hero object, motion
personality, product-surface treatment, and supporting-object arrangement.
Never invent arbitrary variants; there is no hidden randomness or layout based
on copy hashes. See `examples/recipes/metric-proof.yml` and its
`metric-proof-surface-first.yml` sibling.

Plain `check` is browser-free. It performs estimated dwell plus structural
validation and `check --json` returns both `structuralSignature` and
`appearanceSignature`. The structural signature always includes recipe,
recipeVersion, variant, beat sequence, composition family, motif, hero object,
motion personality, product-surface treatment, and supporting-object
arrangement—even for legacy/direct-shot configs.

`preview` and `render` run rendered QA across the entire timeline (15 Hz for
readme-loop/social-film; 12 Hz for product-tour): `qa.text-collision`,
`qa.text-dwell`, `qa.empty-frame`, `qa.static-time`, `qa.loop-continuity`, and
`qa.clipping`. Findings appear under `report.json.renderedQa` and report
warnings. In the first detector release they do not become ordinary check
errors, but `render --strict` blocks atomic promotion when any finding exists.
Never work around a finding by hiding QA markers; fix copy density, layout,
timing, state progression, or loop choreography.

Eval-only pair comparison uses relationship metadata. Distinct-brand pairs need
structural difference plus CIEDE2000 accent delta >= 10 or two appearance
category differences. Same-brand pairs are appearance-exempt. Sibling-product
pairs need structural difference only.

## Authoring guidance

- Reconstruct, don't paste: when handed screenshots, extract the journey and
  rebuild it from synthetic scenes; screenshots are reference, not output.
  Aim for clean, subtly rounded, readable UI; cute but not childish.
- Delight primitives (opt-in, keep them rare): celebrate fires a success burst
  at the climax; chat.avatars adds per-role avatars. Legacy `tap` fields remain
  accepted for config compatibility but do not render a cursor.
- Story arc that works: typing (the ask) -> steps (the work) -> status-card
  (the result) -> hold 1-1.5s so the ending reads before the loop.
- Top-level `cinematic` sets defaults for non-screenshot content scenes. Scene
  `cinematic` blocks override it, holds inherit the held scene, and screenshots
  stay explicit-only through scene-level cinematic plus raw-intentional brief
  policy.
- `cinematic.composition` supports `center-hero` for direct hero emphasis,
  `floating-stage` for a centered floating product surface inside a larger
  stage, and `macro-card` when one result card or panel should become the hero
  object. Use `path-journey` for step-by-step flows where the path itself
  should read visually, and `orbit-object` when the object should feel centered
  inside a subtle orbital stage.
- `cinematic.motion` supports `float-in` for a gentle staged entrance, `rise`
  for a simpler upward reveal, `drift` for a slow ambient hold on a scene meant
  to linger, `settle` for a crisp overshoot that snaps back, and `dolly-in` for
  a hero push-in (eligible only on status-card/metric-card/screen/screenshot).
- `cinematic.ambient: ember` adds a restrained ambient layer inside the frame.
  In v1 the resolved scope is timeline-wide whenever any effective scene
  cinematic opts in; render records this as `cinematic.ambient.scope: timeline`
  in report.json.
- Use `screen.layout: hero` for one centered product result or launch stat,
  `split` for a compact two-column product surface, and the default `stack` for
  dense phone/dashboard flows.
- More arcs: terminal-playback alone sells a CLI; chat (the ask) ->
  code with added/removed (the fix) -> status-card (the PR); metric-card
  closes a launch-post demo with numbers; screen reconstructs dense product
  dashboards and no-screenshot category fallbacks. Match scene to frame:
  terminal-playback + terminal, chat + phone, code/metric-card + browser.
- Rendering examples ship in the package under examples/ (one per scene
  type, plus desktop-app, frameless, and screen-dashboard/screen-focus/
  screen-scroll for product reconstruction, plus transparent-hero for alpha
  cutouts); copy one as a starting point, or start from a gallery template via
  init --template / init --category product.
- A GitHub Action lives at bprateeek/demoframe/action for CI renders
  (README auto-refresh and PR preview recipes in action/README.md).
- Keep total duration 8-15s for README heroes.
- Respect the text limits; check enforces them. Shorter copy reads better at
  280px display width.
- Default transition cut everywhere; one crossfade, push, or dip-to-color into
  the final scene is a nice touch and usually affordable. Use push to step
  forward between peer scenes and dip-to-color to reset the eye before a new
  section; both cost GIF size, so keep them sparse.
- Never put real emails, tokens, internal URLs, or customer data in copy;
  check will warn, --strict will fail.
- Workflow: edit config -> check -> render -> parse report.json -> inspect
  <out>/preview/ stills -> fix and re-render. Use preview/serve for cheaper
  iteration while the config is still changing.

<!-- demoframe:guidance-v2:start -->
## Demos (demoframe)

Screenshots are reference, not ingredients: reconstruct the flow as synthetic
demoframe scenes (`typing`, `steps`, `status-card`, `chat`, `screen`), never
paste screenshots into a frame.

Interview before authoring:

1. Narrative arc: the ask, the work, the result.
2. Climax / money shot: which single moment to land and hold on.
3. Destination: readme, x-post, linkedin, or product-hunt.
4. Brand: accent color, frame type, light or dark.
5. Product and repo names.
6. Copy to feature verbatim (exact labels and titles).
7. Screenshot extraction: preserve, simplify, remove, and exact copy.

Record the answers in `brief`, set `brief.mode: user-confirmed` only after the
user confirms the story and source-to-scene mapping, and fill
audience/source/screenshotPolicy/placement/arc/climax. `--autonomous` allows an
inferred brief only; it never downgrades errors on a user-confirmed brief.

New configs use story v2. Set `brief.story.version: 2`, choose an explicit
`profile` (`readme-loop`, `social-film`, or `product-tour`), and bind:

- `promise` to durable copy that is visibly rendered;
- `proof` to typed ids in `demoframe-context.yml` (`exact`, deterministic
  `formatted`, or user-confirmed-only `paraphrase` with exact display copy);
- ordered beats (`hook`, one or more `build`, one `payoff`, optional `outro`)
  to scenes/shots through `beatId`; recipe mode generates its beat skeleton.

Run `demoframe context init` to scaffold the versioned typed context manifest.
Every source digest covers selected lines or a JSON pointer, so unrelated file
edits do not stale the entry. Keep sources inside the repo; assets need license
and privacy acknowledgement. Use `demoframe check --json` for the stable coded
machine contract.

Legacy scene authoring remains supported: a config with no `brief.story` and no
`profile` stays on legacy behavior and receives no story-v2 narrative errors,
including when `--for` is supplied. Do not add partial story-v2 fields to a
legacy config unless you intend to migrate it.

Choose exactly one authoring source: `scenes`, `shots`, or
`brief.story.recipe`, never more than one. Use
legacy `scenes` for a single full-canvas object per beat. Use direct `shots`
only when the story needs two or more coordinated objects, carry-over, or an
attention-guiding camera move. Every shot needs `id`, `beatId`, `duration`, and
named objects in semantic slots (`hero`, `supporting`, `background`,
`foreground`). Shot objects may embed existing scenes with `kind: scene`, or
use the small semantic registry: `kinetic-text`, `logo-lockup`,
`product-surface`, `hero-metric`, `chart-path`, and local `image`. Use a
manifest-backed `logo-lockup` for visible identity; a bare `theme.logo` is only
a watermark. Local SVG images are sanitized, but still require licensed,
privacy-reviewed source art. Keep the same durable-copy and proof rules.
Object enter/emphasize/exit, camera target,
carry, ambient timing, and transitions must explain state or causality—not add
motion for its own sake. `report.json` records the resolved shot graph and hash.
Do not add cursor objects, orbit/sonar decoration, floating perspective cards,
or a character unless that character materially improves comprehension. If the
user supplies an Excalidraw/SVG character, include it as an `image` object and
keep it subordinate to the product flow.

Use a recipe when its reliable narrative skeleton matches the story:
`code-to-result`, `problem-to-solution`, `workflow-transformation`,
`metric-proof`, `ui-focus-tour`, or `architecture-flow`. Set
`recipeVersion: 1` and choose an explicit recipe-specific variant from the
schema; never invent a string. Recipe mode needs deterministic display copy on
the first proof item. Variants intentionally change composition, motif, hero,
motion, product-surface treatment, or supporting arrangement while preserving
the recipe's beat sequence. There is no random selection and no layout derived
from mutable copy hashes. Inspect `report.json.shotGraph.recipe` to verify the
materialized choice.

Treat `check` and rendered QA as separate gates. Plain `check` never launches a
browser; use its estimated dwell and `--json` structural/appearance signatures
while authoring. `preview` and `render` sample the entire timeline for text
collision, actual dwell, empty/static time, clipping, and loop continuity.
Rendered findings are warnings during their first release, but `render
--strict` blocks atomic promotion. Fix the underlying composition or pacing;
never remove `data-qa-key` coverage or add movement solely to silence a gate.
Eval compares signatures according to pair relationships: distinct brands also
need real appearance distance, while same-brand and sibling-product pairs are
judged on film structure.

Do repo reconnaissance before scenes: inspect the nearest README/app
metadata/routes/examples, identify
product vocabulary, success state, exact copy, and privacy risks, then write:

```md
source signal -> intent -> scene -> preserve / simplify / remove / copy
```

`check`/`render` reject a frameless all-screenshot demo. Use
`--allow-raw-screenshots` only when raw pixels are the subject.
<!-- demoframe:guidance-v2:end -->
